quote: Let X1, X2, ...., Xn be random variables, phi_1 and phi_2 are generators of n-dimentional Archimax copulas C1 and C2 respectively with inverse of phi_2 is psi_2. If psi_2 o phi_1 satisfies the following, (1) Super-additive. (2) For A such that, 1/n <= A <= 1, psi_2 o phi_1 (t . A) >= A psi_2 o phi_1 (t), where A : [0,1]^n -> [1/n, 1] is pickands dependence function as in equation (7). then C1(x) <= C2(x) for all x in [0,1]^n.
family: Archimax copula C_{phi,A}(x) = phi(||psi(x)|| A(psi(x)/||psi(x)||)); phi n-monotone Archimedean generator, A Pickands dependence function
compared: two Archimax copulas C1 (generator phi_1) and C2 (generator phi_2) sharing the same Pickands function A

hypotheses.text: psi_2 o phi_1 satisfies the following, (1) Super-additive.
For A such that, 1/n <= A <= 1, psi_2 o phi_1 (t . A) >= A psi_2 o phi_1 (t)
hypotheses.formal: psi_2(phi_1(A t)) >= A psi_2(phi_1(t)) for A in [1/n,1]

conclusion.direction: C1(x) <= C2(x) for all x in [0,1]^n

ambiguity: Conclusion is a pointwise ordering of copula CDFs (lower-orthant/concordance type), not one of the named univariate stochastic orders; recorded as it orders two distributions.

quote: Suppose (X1, ..., Xn) following PHR(B_bar, alpha; phi_1, A) and (Y1, ..., Yn) following PHR(B_bar, beta; phi_2, A) where phi_1 and phi_2 are Archimedean n-monotone generators for Archimax copula C_{phi_1,A} and C_{phi_2,A} respectively and B_bar the baseline servival function of the model. Then X_{n:n}(alpha; phi_1, A) >=st Y_{n:n}(beta; phi_2, A) if (i) beta <=w alpha, psi_2 o phi_1 is super additive and (ii) psi_2 o phi_1 (t . A) >= A . psi_2 o phi_1 (t).
family: PHR(B_bar, alpha; phi, A): proportional hazards F_bar_{X_i}(x) = B_bar(x)^{alpha_i}, alpha_i > 0, with Archimax copula C_{phi,A}

quote: Consider for illustration of the theorem 4.1, the sample X1, X2, X3, X4, X5 from U(0,1) with n = 4 and n+1 = 5. Now we know that X_{k:n} ~ Beta(k, n+1-k). Now we take l from Gumbel-Hougaard Copula ... as the appropriate stdf for Archimax copula model with 5-monotone Archimedean generator phi(t) = e^{-t^{1/theta}}, theta in [1, infty), where stable tail dependence function (stdf) is l(x) = (x1^theta + ... + xn^theta)^{1/theta} ... For reverse hazard rate ordering, we calculate t phi'(t)/phi(t) = -(1/theta) t^{1/theta} which is a decreasing function of t >= 0, because for theta in [1,infty), we get d/dt(-(1/theta) t^{1/theta}) = -(1/theta^2) t^{1/theta - 1} <= 0 for all t >= 0. On the other hand F_{X5:5}/F_{X4:4} = x, F_{X4:4}/F_{X3:4} = x^4/(4x^3 - 3x^4) and equating both expression of l we have A = n^{1/theta - 1} with n = 4. Plots are shown below which illustrates the theorem 4.1(i) for theta = 4.
